item.title: Gustave Crocodile: Africa's Deadliest Man-Eater
item.description:
Gustave the Crocodile — Is Africa's Most Feared Killer Still Alive?
Gustave the crocodile terrorized the shores of Lake Tanganyika and the Ruzizi River for over three decades, allegedly killing close to 300 people — then he vanished without a trace. Was he ever really just one crocodile, or a legend built from dozens of separate kills?
Herpetologists studying Nile crocodile (Crocodylus niloticus) behavior note that individuals this size — Gustave is estimated near 20 feet and over a ton — are exceptionally rare survivors of decades of unregulated hunting, which helps explain both his size and his uncanny ability to avoid every trap set for him. Peer-reviewed research on crocodilian territorial and ambush behavior helps explain how one apex predator could evade capture for 30+ years while returning to the same hunting grounds.
In this documentary we break down the recorded attacks, the failed capture expeditions, and what wildlife biologists actually know about Gustave's disappearance — plus why some researchers believe the "legend" may conceal more than one crocodile. This is the real science behind Africa's most feared apex predator.
